publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: THE ROLE OF THE HIPPOCAMPUS IN PROCESSING AUDITORY INFORMATION, AND HOW THE HIPPOCAMPUS ITSELF IS SHAPED BY SOUND
span.quote: The hippocampus has a well-established role in spatial and episodic memory but a broader function has been proposed including aspects of perception and relational processing. Neural bases of sound analysis have been described in the pathway to auditory cortex, but wider networks supporting auditory cognition are still being established. We review what is known about the role of the hippocampus in processing auditory information, and how the hippocampus itself is shaped by sound. In examining imaging, recording, and lesion studies in species from rodents to humans, we uncover a hierarchy of hippocampal responses to sound including during passive exposure, active listening, and the learning of associations between sounds and other stimuli. We describe how the hippocampus' connectivity and computational architecture allow it to track and manipulate auditory information – whether in the form of speech, music, or environmental, emotional, or phantom sounds. Functional and structural correlates of auditory experience are also identified. The extent of auditory-hippocampal interactions is consistent with the view that the hippocampus makes broad contributions to perception and cognition, beyond spatial and episodic memory.

span.label: whether a structure known for spatial and episodic memory belongs in an account of hearing at all - GIVEN THE TWO MOST WELL-KNOWN FUNCTIONS OF THE HIPPOCAMPUS, A REVIEW OF THIS STRUCTURE IN RELATION TO SOUND MAY SEEM AN UNLIKELY EXERCISE
span.quote: Given the two most well-known functions of the hippocampus – supporting episodic memory in humans ( Scoville and Milner, 1957 , Squire and Zola-Morgan, 1991 ) and spatial navigation in animals ( O’Keefe and Dostrovsky, 1971 ) – a review of this structure in relation to sound may seem an unlikely exercise.

span.label: A HIERARCHY OF HIPPOCAMPAL RESPONSES TO SOUND INCLUDING DURING PASSIVE EXPOSURE, ACTIVE LISTENING, AND THE LEARNING OF ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN SOUNDS AND OTHER STIMULI
span.quote: The hippocampus has a well-established role in spatial and episodic memory but a broader function has been proposed including aspects of perception and relational processing. span.label: existence
span.quote: The extent of auditory-hippocampal interactions is consistent with the view that the hippocampus makes broad contributions to perception and cognition, beyond spatial and episodic memory.

span.label: auditory-hippocampal interactions
span.quote: We review what is known about the role of the hippocampus in processing auditory information, and how the hippocampus itself is shaped by sound.

span.label: review
span.quote: Recording, imaging and lesion studies are reviewed in species from mouse to human.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Subcortical routes deliver a fast, non-selective signal that a sound is present, while slower cortical routes deliver elaborated, meaning-bearing representations — explaining why some hippocampal responses precede auditory cortex and scale with intensity rather than identity
span.quote: These subcortical pathways may provide fast, indiscriminate communication of the presence of sound, in contrast to slower cortical routes conveying more elaborated representations of a sound and its meaning, including after integrating information from other sensory modalities ( Rolls, 1996 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The hippocampus acts as a comparator: CA3 sends a prediction to CA1, where it is matched against entorhinal sensory input, and the mismatch generates the observed violation and surprise responses
span.quote: Violation and surprise responses in hippocampus are consistent with it acting as a comparator, with predictions passed from CA3 to CA1 where they are combined with sensory input from entorhinal cortex ( Hasselmo and Wyble, 1997 , Lisman and Grace, 2005 , Vinogradova, 1975b , Vinogradova, 2001 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Acoustically boosting sleep slow oscillations accelerates consolidation of prior memories to cortex, which releases hippocampal capacity and thereby improves encoding of new material the next day
span.quote: This may indicate that boosting slow oscillations allowed previous memories to be consolidated to cortex, freeing up hippocampal resources for subsequent encoding.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: During musical 'chills' the nucleus accumbens becomes more active and its inhibitory projections suppress hippocampal blood flow, producing the observed decrease rather than increase
span.quote: This reduced response is thought to arise through inhibitory projections from the nucleus accumbens, part of the dopaminergic reward system in which activity increases during chills.

span.label: the widened job description that makes the question askable: ONE IDEA IS THAT THE HIPPOCAMPUS IS IMPORTANT FOR THE BINDING OF ARBITRARY RELATIONS AND MEDIATING THEIR FLEXIBLE EXPRESSION - THIS EXTENDED JOB DESCRIPTION ENCOMPASSES LINKING MULTIMODAL OBJECTS WITH A SPATIOTEMPORAL, ENVIRONMENTAL, OR COGNITIVE CONTEXT, SUPPORTING SHORT-TERM MEMORY, ASSOCIATING DISPARATE ELEMENTS OF A SCENE, STRUCTURING CONCEPTUAL KNOWLEDGE, AND FORMING PREDICTIONS
span.quote: However, theories of hippocampal function have long extended beyond episodic memory and spatial navigation ( Kimble, 1968 , Papez, 1937 ). One idea is that the hippocampus is important for the binding of arbitrary relations and mediating their flexible expression ( Cohen and Eichenbaum, 1993 , Lisman et al., 2017 ). This extended job description encompasses linking multimodal objects with a spatiotemporal, environmental, or cognitive context to form episodic memories ( Yonelinas et al., 2019 ), supporting short-term memory ( Hannula and Ranganath, 2008 , Pertzov et al., 2013 ), associating disparate elements of a scene ( Graham et al., 2010 , Maguire and Mullally, 2013 , Olsen et al., 2012 ), structuring conceptual knowledge ( Behrens et al., 2018 ), and forming predictions

span.label: and the conclusion drawn from it: IN LIGHT OF THIS EXTENDED PROPOSED FUNCTIONAL SCOPE, A FULL ACCOUNT OF THE AUDITORY SYSTEM SHOULD AT LEAST CONSIDER THE HIPPOCAMPUS
span.quote: In light of this extended proposed functional scope, a full account of the auditory system should at least consider the hippocampus.

span.label: the clinical result that the review is built towards: CLICK TRAINS PRESENTED AT THIS RATE (BUT NOT WITH RANDOM TIMING) REDUCED SIGNS OF ALZHEIMER'S PATHOLOGY (AMYLOID LOAD AND TAU PHOSPHORYLATION) IN THE HIPPOCAMPUS OF THIS MOUSE MODEL AND BOOSTED MEMORY FOR THE IDENTITY AND LOCATION OF OBJECTS
span.quote: Remarkably, click trains presented at this rate (but not with random timing) reduced signs of Alzheimer's pathology (amyloid load and tau phosphorylation) in the hippocampus of this mouse model and boosted memory for the identity and location of objects.

span.label: The review deliberately does not attempt an integrated theory of hippocampal function, aiming only to map the circumstances in which the hippocampus processes and is shaped by sound.
span.quote: However, rather than attempting an integrated theory of the hippocampus through the prism of sound, our aim is to highlight the range of circumstances under which it processes and is shaped by auditory signals.

span.label: Hippocampal computational principles are covered only to the extent that they account for auditory data.
span.quote: We describe known computational principles of the hippocampus to the extent that they account for auditory data.

span.label: The authors do not claim the hippocampus is an auditory structure, only that its computational architecture may be engaged and altered by auditory tasks.
span.quote: In essence, we are not "claiming" the hippocampus as an auditory structure so much as examining how its computational architecture might be engaged in and altered by auditory tasks.

span.label: the anatomy points the other way - IN HUMANS, CORTICAL CIRCUITS UNDERLYING AUDITORY PERCEPTION AND COGNITION ARE LARGELY FOUND IN LATERAL, RATHER THAN MEDIAL TEMPORAL LOBE STRUCTURES
span.quote: In humans, cortical circuits underlying auditory perception and cognition are largely found in lateral, rather than medial temporal lobe structures

span.label: and the specific claim has been contested - the ROLE IN AUDITORY MEMORY IN PRIMATES HAS BEEN CHALLENGED ON ANATOMICAL AND FUNCTIONAL GROUNDS
span.quote: role in auditory memory in primates has been challenged on anatomical and functional grounds

span.label: the volume-function relationship does not generalize - FOR SPATIAL NAVIGATION AND OTHER HIPPOCAMPUS-DEPENDENT TASKS, THE GENERALIZABILITY OF A VOLUME-FUNCTION RELATIONSHIP TO A NON-EXPERT POPULATION HAS NOT BEEN DEMONSTRATED
span.quote: For spatial navigation and other hippocampus-dependent tasks, the generalizability of a volume-function relationship to a non-expert population has not been demonstrated

span.label: and the structure the argument is about was not the one measured - THE VOLUME OF PARAHIPPOCAMPAL GYRUS (HIPPOCAMPUS WAS NOT TESTED) WAS FOUND TO CORRELATE POSITIVELY WITH AN INDEX OF MUSICAL SOPHISTICATION
span.quote: However with respect to music, the volume of parahippocampal gyrus (hippocampus was not tested) was found to correlate positively with an index of musical sophistication in a group of 73 older adults after controlling for intracranial volume

span.label: the direction of the relationships is not established - LONGITUDINAL STUDIES, SIMILAR TO THOSE IN TAXI DRIVERS, WILL BE IMPORTANT TO ESTABLISH CAUSALITY IN ANY OF THE ABOVE RELATIONSHIPS
span.quote: Longitudinal studies, similar to those in taxi drivers ( Woollett and Maguire, 2011 ), will be important to establish causality in any of the above relationships.

span.label: and the mechanism of the headline clinical effect is open - THE MECHANISM IS NOT YET UNDERSTOOD
span.quote: The implications for dementia treatment are considerable, and work is ongoing to test the same approach in human trials ( Chan et al., 2021 ). The mechanism is not yet understood but networks of inhibitory interneurons generate peaks at this low-gamma frequency, which may also be involved in coupling CA3 and CA1 during memory retrieval

span.label: IT REMAINS TO BE DETERMINED WHETHER SOUNDS PREDICTED ON THE BASIS OF ASSOCIATIONS LEARNED IN THE SHORT-TERM OR THROUGH SEMANTIC CONTEXT CAN BE DECODED FROM HIPPOCAMPAL ACTIVITY BEFORE THEY ARE HEARD
span.quote: It remains to be determined whether sounds predicted on the basis of associations learned in the short-term (such as the next note in a melody learned in an experiment) or through semantic context (such as the sound of a bark following a picture of a dog) can be decoded from hippocampal activity before they are heard.

span.label: the definition of a perceptual object - AN AUDITORY PERCEPTUAL OBJECT, LIKE ITS VISUAL COUNTERPARTS, IS DEFINED BY THE BINDING OF MULTIPLE SENSORY FEATURES, REPRESENTS A SOURCE DISTINCT FROM OTHERS IN THE SCENE, AND IS INVARIANT OVER DIFFERENT SENSORY INSTANCES
span.quote: An auditory perceptual object, like its visual counterparts, is defined by the binding of multiple sensory features, represents a source distinct from others in the scene, and is invariant over different sensory instances

span.label: the volume-function logic of the taxi-driver finding, applied to musicians and piano-tuners - POSITIVE RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN YEARS OF TRAINING AND ANTERIOR HIPPOCAMPAL GRAY MATTER VOLUME
span.quote: Such associations have been found, with positive relationships between years of training and anterior hippocampal gray matter volume in musicians ( Groussard et al., 2014 , Groussard et al., 2010a ) and piano-tuners

span.label: the behavioral report moved to the end of a trial or block
span.quote: In human subjects, behavioral relevance can be instilled in the absence of explicit reward through task instructions, such as to count particular target sounds or to make certain judgments. By having subjects report target counts at the end of a trial or block, explicit motor confounds are removed.

span.label: the stimulus rate varied against a timing-matched control
span.quote: Remarkably, click trains presented at this rate (but not with random timing) reduced signs of Alzheimer's pathology (amyloid load and tau phosphorylation) in the hippocampus of this mouse model and boosted memory for the identity and location of objects.

span.label: intracranial volume controlled for in the structural correlation
span.quote: However with respect to music, the volume of parahippocampal gyrus (hippocampus was not tested) was found to correlate positively with an index of musical sophistication in a group of 73 older adults after controlling for intracranial volume

span.label: THE REVIEW EXISTS BECAUSE OF WHAT THE STRUCTURE IS NAMED FOR, AND SAYS SO IN ITS FIRST SENTENCE: GIVEN THE TWO MOST WELL-KNOWN FUNCTIONS OF THE HIPPOCAMPUS - SUPPORTING EPISODIC MEMORY IN HUMANS AND SPATIAL NAVIGATION IN ANIMALS - A REVIEW OF THIS STRUCTURE IN RELATION TO SOUND MAY SEEM AN UNLIKELY EXERCISE. What is not looked for in a structure is decided by what the structure is known for
span.quote: Given the two most well-known functions of the hippocampus – supporting episodic memory in humans ( Scoville and Milner, 1957 , Squire and Zola-Morgan, 1991 ) and spatial navigation in animals ( O’Keefe and Dostrovsky, 1971 ) – a review of this structure in relation to sound may seem an unlikely exercise.

span.label: and the anatomy points away too: IN HUMANS, CORTICAL CIRCUITS UNDERLYING AUDITORY PERCEPTION AND COGNITION ARE LARGELY FOUND IN LATERAL, RATHER THAN MEDIAL TEMPORAL LOBE STRUCTURES
span.quote: In humans, cortical circuits underlying auditory perception and cognition are largely found in lateral, rather than medial temporal lobe structures

span.label: THE QUESTION BECOMES ASKABLE ONLY BY WIDENING THE JOB DESCRIPTION: THEORIES OF HIPPOCAMPAL FUNCTION HAVE LONG EXTENDED BEYOND EPISODIC MEMORY AND SPATIAL NAVIGATION - THE HIPPOCAMPUS IS IMPORTANT FOR THE BINDING OF ARBITRARY RELATIONS AND MEDIATING THEIR FLEXIBLE EXPRESSION. Widen the function and the evidence that was always there becomes relevant
span.quote: However, theories of hippocampal function have long extended beyond episodic memory and spatial navigation ( Kimble, 1968 , Papez, 1937 ). One idea is that the hippocampus is important for the binding of arbitrary relations and mediating their flexible expression ( Cohen and Eichenbaum, 1993 , Lisman et al., 2017 ). This extended job description encompasses linking multimodal objects with a spatiotemporal, environmental, or cognitive context to form episodic memories ( Yonelinas et al., 2019 ), supporting short-term memory ( Hannula and Ranganath, 2008 , Pertzov et al., 2013 ), associating disparate elements of a scene ( Graham et al., 2010 , Maguire and Mullally, 2013 , Olsen et al., 2012 ), structuring conceptual knowledge ( Behrens et al., 2018 ), and forming predictions

span.label: and the conclusion follows from the widening rather than from new data: IN LIGHT OF THIS EXTENDED PROPOSED FUNCTIONAL SCOPE, A FULL ACCOUNT OF THE AUDITORY SYSTEM SHOULD AT LEAST CONSIDER THE HIPPOCAMPUS
span.quote: In light of this extended proposed functional scope, a full account of the auditory system should at least consider the hippocampus.

span.label: THE POOLING ACROSS SPECIES IS ARGUED FOR, NOT ASSUMED: RECOGNIZING THE RELATIVE PRESERVATION OF HIPPOCAMPAL ANATOMY AND PHYSIOLOGY ACROSS SPECIES, AND THE ADVANCES IN UNDERSTANDING FUNCTION THIS AFFORDS, WE INCLUDE STUDIES FROM RODENTS TO PRIMATES - ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICAL AND NEUROIMAGING DATA ARE CONSIDERED ALONGSIDE NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL AND ANIMAL LESION WORK
span.quote: Recognizing the relative preservation of hippocampal anatomy and physiology across species, and the advances in understanding function this affords ( Buffalo, 2015 , Clark and Squire, 2013 , Cohen and Eichenbaum, 1993 , Witter and Amaral, 2021 ), we include studies from rodents to primates. Electrophysiological and neuroimaging data are considered alongside neuropsychological and animal lesion work.

span.label: A DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN STUDIES ATTRIBUTED TO ONE PARAMETER OF THE ANALYSIS: DIFFERENCES ACROSS THE RESULTS OF THESE STUDIES MAY RELATE TO THE THRESHOLDS USED IN THE PROBABILISTIC TRACTOGRAPHY PROCEDURE
span.quote: Differences across the results of these studies may relate to the thresholds used in the probabilistic tractography procedure. Complementing structural approaches like DTI that identify anatomical tracts, functional-connectivity analysis defines correlated time series between areas, from which direct or indirect connections can be inferred.

span.label: A DEFINITION WIDENED, EXPLICITLY: A BROADER DEFINITION OF CONTEXT IS ADOPTED IN THE CONTEXTUAL BINDING THEORY OF HUMAN EPISODIC MEMORY - IT HOLDS THAT NOT ONLY BACKGROUND ELEMENTS OF THE PHYSICAL ENVIRONMENT, BUT ALSO SLOWLY CHANGING COGNITIVE STATE OR MOOD AS WELL AS TEMPORAL CONTEXT, ARE BOUND TOGETHER IN THE HIPPOCAMPUS. The same word, a larger set, and the older findings are now about the new one
span.quote: A broader definition of context is adopted in the contextual binding theory of human episodic memory ( Yonelinas et al., 2019 ; see also Section 13 ). It holds that not only background elements of the physical environment, but also slowly changing cognitive state or mood as well as temporal context, are bound together in the hippocampus with items and events as they are encountered or experienced

span.label: AND A DEFINITION IMPORTED FROM ANOTHER SENSE: AN AUDITORY PERCEPTUAL OBJECT, LIKE ITS VISUAL COUNTERPARTS, IS DEFINED BY THE BINDING OF MULTIPLE SENSORY FEATURES, REPRESENTS A SOURCE DISTINCT FROM OTHERS IN THE SCENE, AND IS INVARIANT OVER DIFFERENT SENSORY INSTANCES
span.quote: An auditory perceptual object, like its visual counterparts, is defined by the binding of multiple sensory features, represents a source distinct from others in the scene, and is invariant over different sensory instances

span.label: OPPOSITE SINGLE-UNIT FINDINGS IN ONE STRUCTURE: single unit recordings from human hippocampus REVEAL NEURONS THAT RESPOND PREFERENTIALLY TO REPEATED WORDS ALONGSIDE THOSE DRIVEN BY WORD NOVELTY - a `hippocampus signals novelty` tag and a `hippocampus signals repetition` tag are both true of the same recordings
span.quote: The novelty of both a word ( Davis et al., 2009 ) and its category ( Dolan and Fletcher, 1997 ) can drive hippocampal activity during memory encoding. However single unit recordings from human hippocampus reveal neurons that respond preferentially to repeated words alongside those driven by word novelty

span.label: A STRUCTURAL CORRELATION WHOSE CAUSAL READING IS WITHHELD: LONGITUDINAL STUDIES, SIMILAR TO THOSE IN TAXI DRIVERS, WILL BE IMPORTANT TO ESTABLISH CAUSALITY IN ANY OF THE ABOVE RELATIONSHIPS

span.label: and it does not generalize beyond experts: FOR SPATIAL NAVIGATION AND OTHER HIPPOCAMPUS-DEPENDENT TASKS, THE GENERALIZABILITY OF A VOLUME-FUNCTION RELATIONSHIP TO A NON-EXPERT POPULATION HAS NOT BEEN DEMONSTRATED
span.quote: For spatial navigation and other hippocampus-dependent tasks, the generalizability of a volume-function relationship to a non-expert population has not been demonstrated

span.label: THE FINDING CITED FOR A STRUCTURE WAS MEASURED IN A DIFFERENT ONE, AND THE REVIEW SAYS SO IN A PARENTHESIS: THE VOLUME OF PARAHIPPOCAMPAL GYRUS (HIPPOCAMPUS WAS NOT TESTED) WAS FOUND TO CORRELATE POSITIVELY WITH AN INDEX OF MUSICAL SOPHISTICATION IN A GROUP OF 73 OLDER ADULTS AFTER CONTROLLING FOR INTRACRANIAL VOLUME

span.label: and the effect is larger when a second modality is added: EFFECTS WERE LARGER WHEN THE AUDITORY STIMULUS WAS PAIRED WITH VISUAL FLICKER AT THE SAME RATE - THIS COMBINED STIMULATION ALSO INDUCED AN INCREASE IN 40 Hz POWER AND A CLUSTERING EFFECT OF MICROGLIA AROUND AMYLOID DEPOSITS

span.label: THE MECHANISM OF THE HEADLINE RESULT IS NOT UNDERSTOOD, AND HUMAN TRIALS ARE ALREADY RUNNING: WORK IS ONGOING TO TEST THE SAME APPROACH IN HUMAN TRIALS - THE MECHANISM IS NOT YET UNDERSTOOD

span.quote: The extent of auditory-hippocampal interactions is consistent with the view that the hippocampus makes broad contributions to perception and cognition, beyond spatial and episodic memory.

span.label: MULTIPLE PATHWAYS ARE AVAILABLE FOR AUDITORY INFORMATION TO REACH THE HIPPOCAMPUS, AND FOR THE HIPPOCAMPUS IN TURN TO INFLUENCE ACTIVITY AT CANONICAL AUDITORY STRUCTURES
span.quote: In sum, multiple pathways are available for auditory information to reach the hippocampus, and for the hippocampus in turn to influence activity at canonical auditory structures.

span.label: Habituation to repeated behaviorally irrelevant sound is unusually strong in hippocampus relative to other structures.
span.quote: Although habituation to a repeated auditory stimulus is a widespread neural phenomenon ( Bickford et al., 1993 , Miller and Freedman, 1993 , Moxon et al., 1999 , Picton et al., 1976 ), it is particularly pronounced in hippocampus, at least for behaviorally irrelevant input in rodents and rabbits ( Bickford-Wimer et al., 1990 , Vinogradova, 1975b ).

span.label: The review finds no demonstrated causal role for hippocampus in forming auditory objects, marking that account as speculative.
span.quote: These ideas remain mostly speculative, and a critical role for hippocampus in auditory object formation has not been demonstrated.

span.label: The proposal that theta phase precession could carry auditory sequences is identified as untested.
span.quote: Direct experimental support for this kind of auditory phase precession is currently lacking.

span.label: GIVEN THE TWO MOST WELL-KNOWN FUNCTIONS OF THE HIPPOCAMPUS, A REVIEW OF THIS STRUCTURE IN RELATION TO SOUND MAY SEEM AN UNLIKELY EXERCISE
span.quote: Given the two most well-known functions of the hippocampus – supporting episodic memory in humans ( Scoville and Milner, 1957 , Squire and Zola-Morgan, 1991 ) and spatial navigation in animals ( O’Keefe and Dostrovsky, 1971 ) – a review of this structure in relation to sound may seem an unlikely exercise.

span.label: IN HUMANS, CORTICAL CIRCUITS UNDERLYING AUDITORY PERCEPTION AND COGNITION ARE LARGELY FOUND IN LATERAL, RATHER THAN MEDIAL TEMPORAL LOBE STRUCTURES
span.quote: In humans, cortical circuits underlying auditory perception and cognition are largely found in lateral, rather than medial temporal lobe structures

span.label: DIFFERENCES ACROSS THE RESULTS OF THESE STUDIES MAY RELATE TO THE THRESHOLDS USED IN THE PROBABILISTIC TRACTOGRAPHY PROCEDURE
span.quote: Differences across the results of these studies may relate to the thresholds used in the probabilistic tractography procedure. Complementing structural approaches like DTI that identify anatomical tracts, functional-connectivity analysis defines correlated time series between areas, from which direct or indirect connections can be inferred.

span.label: single unit recordings from human hippocampus REVEAL NEURONS THAT RESPOND PREFERENTIALLY TO REPEATED WORDS ALONGSIDE THOSE DRIVEN BY WORD NOVELTY
span.quote: The novelty of both a word ( Davis et al., 2009 ) and its category ( Dolan and Fletcher, 1997 ) can drive hippocampal activity during memory encoding. However single unit recordings from human hippocampus reveal neurons that respond preferentially to repeated words alongside those driven by word novelty

span.label: CLICK TRAINS PRESENTED AT THIS RATE (BUT NOT WITH RANDOM TIMING) REDUCED SIGNS OF ALZHEIMER'S PATHOLOGY (AMYLOID LOAD AND TAU PHOSPHORYLATION) IN THE HIPPOCAMPUS OF THIS MOUSE MODEL
span.quote: Remarkably, click trains presented at this rate (but not with random timing) reduced signs of Alzheimer's pathology (amyloid load and tau phosphorylation) in the hippocampus of this mouse model and boosted memory for the identity and location of objects.

span.label: EFFECTS WERE LARGER WHEN THE AUDITORY STIMULUS WAS PAIRED WITH VISUAL FLICKER AT THE SAME RATE
span.quote: Effects were larger when the auditory stimulus was paired with visual flicker at the same rate - this combined stimulation also induced an increase in 40 Hz power and a clustering effect of microglia around amyloid deposits.

span.label: THE VOLUME OF PARAHIPPOCAMPAL GYRUS (HIPPOCAMPUS WAS NOT TESTED) WAS FOUND TO CORRELATE POSITIVELY WITH AN INDEX OF MUSICAL SOPHISTICATION IN A GROUP OF 73 OLDER ADULTS AFTER CONTROLLING FOR INTRACRANIAL VOLUME
span.quote: However with respect to music, the volume of parahippocampal gyrus (hippocampus was not tested) was found to correlate positively with an index of musical sophistication in a group of 73 older adults after controlling for intracranial volume

span.label: THE GENERALIZABILITY OF A VOLUME-FUNCTION RELATIONSHIP TO A NON-EXPERT POPULATION HAS NOT BEEN DEMONSTRATED
span.quote: For spatial navigation and other hippocampus-dependent tasks, the generalizability of a volume-function relationship to a non-expert population has not been demonstrated

span.label: auditory perceptual object
span.quote: An auditory perceptual object, like its visual counterparts, is defined by the binding of multiple sensory features, represents a source distinct from others in the scene, and is invariant over different sensory instances ( Bizley and Cohen, 2013 , Griffiths and Warren, 2004 , Kubovy and Van Valkenburg, 2001 ).

span.label: pattern separation
span.quote: Pattern separation refers to the storing of distinct activity patterns for memories that share similar features.

span.label: pattern completion
span.quote: The other concept, pattern completion, refers to the retrieval of a memory on the basis of a partial cue, thought to be supported by auto-associative or attractor networks in CA3 ( Rolls, 2013 ).

span.label: delay conditioning vs. trace conditioning
span.quote: As mentioned earlier, whereas animals with hippocampal lesions are able to learn the association between a conditioned stimulus and unconditioned stimulus if these are presented in an overlapping or abutting fashion (“delay conditioning”), the insertion of a silent interval between the two (“trace conditioning”) renders these animals impaired.

span.label: successor representation
span.quote: Related is the idea of the hippocampus as a predictive (not merely spatial) map ( Gershman, 2018 , Stachenfeld et al., 2017 ) that encodes successor representations, namely predictions of future states (discounted future occupancy) given an animal’s current state ( Dayan, 1993 , Momennejad, 2020 ).

span.label: phase precession
span.quote: There is a systematic change in the phase of theta oscillations at which a place cell fires as the animal moves through its firing field (“phase precession”; O’Keefe and Recce, 1993 in rodents; Qasim et al., 2021 in humans).

span.label: tinnitus
span.quote: Tinnitus (see Supplementary Table L) usually takes the form of a low-intensity, high-frequency ringing or white noise that is typically readily masked by environmental sounds but can be chronic and emotionally distressing ( Jastreboff, 1990 ).

span.label: context
span.quote: A broader definition of context is adopted in the contextual binding theory of human episodic memory ( Yonelinas et al., 2019 ; see also Section 13 ). It holds that not only background elements of the physical environment, but also slowly changing cognitive state or mood as well as temporal context, are bound together in the hippocampus with items and events as they are encountered or experienced

span.label: approximately a quarter — Proportion of recorded CA1 cells that carried both a tone-frequency firing field and a spatial place field in the same animals
span.quote: Of all CA1 cells recorded, approximately a quarter had auditory and place fields, a half one or the other, and a quarter neither.

span.label: 740 ms — Average lead time by which hippocampal activity preceded predictive recall activity in auditory cortex during a repeated spoken story
span.quote: At peaks of this predictive measure, mutual information between the auditory cortical high-gamma activity and lower frequency activity in hippocampus was maximal, with hippocampus leading cortical activity by an average of 740 ms ( Fig. 4 E).

span.label: 10 ms — Earliest latency of auditory cortex responses in Heschl's gyrus to single-pulse electrical stimulation of hippocampus in humans
span.quote: In the latter case these occur not only in auditory association areas on the lateral temporal lobe ( Catenoix et al., 2011 , Enatsu et al., 2015 ) but also primary auditory cortex in Heschl's gyrus, with initial responses as early as 10 ms ( Rocchi et al., 2021 ).

span.label: 30–150 Hz — The acoustic 'roughness' rate range whose energy is linked to aversiveness and to neuronal synchronisation in hippocampus and insula
span.quote: Negative reactions to certain sounds may relate to the energy in the “roughness” range of 30–150 Hz; click trains presented at this rate are rated as highly salient and aversive and bring about neuronal synchronization at the presentation rate, particularly in the hippocampus and insula ( Arnal et al., 2019 ).

span.label: 4–7 Hz — Frequency band of rodent hippocampal theta oscillations propagated across cortex
span.quote: The hippocampus orchestrates activity across cortex, propagating theta oscillations (4–7 Hz in rodents) for temporal control of information processing, and sharp-wave ripples for memory consolidation ( Buzsáki, 2015 , Buzsáki, 2002 ; see Section 8 ).
